However, during her admission, she developed severe sudden shoulder pain and altered sensation of the left upper limb, which prompted the multidisciplinary team to aim for urgent surgical resection.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old African female with HIV (CD4 390, virally suppressed on tenofovir-lamivudine-dolutegravir) presented with recently diagnosed hypertension and classic catecholamine excess symptoms including paroxysmal headaches, palpitations, and sweating. Initial evaluation revealed tachycardia (110 bpm) and elevated blood pressure (160/90 mmHg). Biochemical investigation demonstrated markedly elevated 24-hour urine normetanephrines (50,060 nmol/24h; reference 562–2129 nmol/24h). Anatomical localization via CT imaging showed a normal abdomen but identified a large avidly enhancing left posterior mediastinal T1–T3 paraspinal soft tissue mass with extension into the T2 vertebral body and intervertebral neural foramen causing spinal cord abutment. Pre-operative 68Ga DOTATATE scan confirmed somatostatin receptor avidity in the mediastinal mass. The patient underwent 14 days of alpha-blockade (doxazosin) and 72 hours of beta-blockade (atenolol) before emergency T2–T4 laminectomy and posterior resection, which was necessitated by the development of severe sudden shoulder pain and altered sensation in the left upper limb during admission. Histopathological examination revealed a nested (zellballen) growth pattern with capsular invasion and lymphovascular space invasion. Immunohistochemistry was diffusely positive for chromogranin, and the tumor was classified as a well-differentiated paraganglioma with a GAPP (Grading of Adrenal Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma) score of 1. Postoperative assessment at 6 weeks demonstrated persistent catecholamine excess with urine normetanephrines of 66,124 nmol/24h, and MIBG scintigraphy confirmed avid residual disease in the left upper thoracic region.

final.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old African female with HIV (CD4 390, virally suppressed on tenofovir-lamivudine-dolutegravir) presented with recently diagnosed hypertension and classic catecholamine excess symptoms including paroxysmal headaches, palpitations, and sweating. Initial evaluation revealed tachycardia (110 bpm) and elevated blood pressure (160/90 mmHg). Biochemical investigation demonstrated markedly elevated 24-hour urine normetanephrines (50,060 nmol/24h; reference 562–2129 nmol/24h). Anatomical localization via CT imaging showed a normal abdomen but identified a large avidly enhancing left posterior mediastinal T1–T3 paraspinal soft tissue mass with extension into the T2 vertebral body and intervertebral neural foramen causing spinal cord abutment. Pre-operative 68Ga DOTATATE scan confirmed somatostatin receptor avidity in the mediastinal mass. The patient underwent 14 days of alpha-blockade (doxazosin) and 72 hours of beta-blockade (atenolol) before emergency T2–T4 laminectomy and posterior resection, which was necessitated by the development of severe sudden shoulder pain and altered sensation in the left upper limb during admission. Histopathological examination revealed a nested (zellballen) growth pattern with capsular invasion and lymphovascular space invasion. Immunohistochemistry was diffusely positive for chromogranin, and the tumor was classified as a well-differentiated paraganglioma with a GAPP (Grading of Adrenal Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma) score of 1. Postoperative assessment at 6 weeks demonstrated persistent catecholamine excess with urine normetanephrines of 66,124 nmol/24h, and MIBG scintigraphy confirmed avid residual disease in the left upper thoracic region.
